answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral and links equivocation evidence across identities: if k coordinated agents sign conflicting histories, aggregate penalties grow as O(k^2), making collusion progressively uneconomic. Upon detection, controlling the swarm incurs an exponential multiplier in capital loss, while asymmetric depreciation prevents recovery. Thus, a shale garden cannot conceal an island of cheaply replicated validators.
